science.title: How cells use alternative genetic instructions to produce 'shadowing proteins'
science.summary: The human genome contains tens of thousands of genes that provide instructions for making the proteins responsible for carrying out essential functions throughout the body. But those instructions may be more versatile than scientists once understood.

science.title: How M.C. Escher’s Art Creates Bizarre Mathematical Worlds

science.title: How electrons find their way to diamond's quantum defects
science.summary: A diamond's most useful quantum properties come from defects, places where the regular arrangement of carbon atoms is broken. One of these, a nitrogen atom situated next to a vacancy caused by a missing carbon atom, has become a key component in quantum technology.

science.title: The quantum computing race is becoming a deployment race

Since 1976, we have known that the answer is "yes"—but how do you actually find the coloring? science.title: Using a microwave link to transfer a three-level quantum state
science.summary: Quantum technologies, devices and systems that process, store, transfer or collect information leveraging the laws of quantum mechanics, could outperform their classical counterparts on some real-world tasks. Many of these technologies encode quantum information in qubits, which can exist in either of two basic states or a superposition of them.

This means radio signals will take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft, now nearly 50 years into its mission. science.title: Quantum-gas microscope resolves the 'color' of individual atoms in a single shot
science.summary: In 2024, researchers at the Ultracold Quantum Gases group at ICFO built a quantum-gas microscope capable of imaging individual atoms in strontium quantum gases for the first time, marking a key enabling step for quantum simulation. At that time, the researchers imaged strontium-84, a boson that has no spin.

science.title: Rapid-scan satellite data offer clues to typhoon intensity
science.summary: Between 1970 and 2019, tropical cyclones killed nearly 780,000 people worldwide and caused approximately $1.4 trillion in economic losses. As coastal populations continue to grow and climate continues to change, accurate forecasting is essential for saving lives and reducing economic damage.

science.title: 10 desk upgrade gifts to improve PC work and gaming spaces
science.summary: These 10 devices can make the desk space around a PC more versatile, enjoyable, and productive experience.

science.title: How one nuclear blast could cripple nearly every satellite in low Earth orbit
science.summary: We rely on satellites every day for communications, weather forecasts and security, and more than 13,000 are currently circling the planet in low Earth orbit. But they could be more vulnerable than previously thought. Researchers have found that a single nuclear explosion in space could disable almost all of them.

science.title: Quantum observers can 'agree to disagree,' but within limits, new theorem shows
science.summary: Two observers can start with the same description of a quantum system, follow the same probability rules and still disagree about the chance of the same outcome—even while being certain of each other's assessments.

science.title: Meta-compass: An on-chip toolkit for visualizing optical spectrum and polarization
science.summary: A ruler turns length into a position on a scale. A thermometer converts temperature into the height of a liquid column. In each case, a physical quantity becomes easier to read because an instrument gives it a visible reference. We wanted to bring the same idea to light, whose properties are usually measured with separate optical components and then interpreted through additional data processing.
